title: Wickliffe in Milwaukee and his kindness to Levy
summary: Wickliffe played Milwaukee around 1917 as a Ginger Band because the city banned the word jazz. He encouraged Levy as a young violinist.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Now, they tell me Wycliffe played Milwaukee in about 1917. That was Darnell's first job, didn't they?
Yes, and Darnell had to put long pants on to play the job.
And they called it Wycliffe's Jazz Band, and the city wouldn't allow him to put up that song.

Word jazz, and he called it the Ginger Band. Your information is perfect because, excuse me, I know Wycliffe. Wycliffe was kind of fond of me because he had seen me come up with the violin. We had roomed at the same place, you know, and he heard me practicing, and he'd say, You're going to make it. He says, You'll make it. And so a year later, I was in his band. And he told me a lot of things. A lot of things encouraged me, and told me that Clarence Lee was a wonderful violinist, but when he got a little too much money, it was hard to handle or something like that. Or he tried to play too many women or something. And Wycliffe was very nice to me.
